text: The presence of rigidity, mild hand tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your progressive walking difficulty, incontinence, and slurred speech strongly suggests Parkinsonian features and autonomic involvement. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C).

The clinical picture of progressive parkinsonism (rigidity, tremor), autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence), and bulbar symptoms (slurred speech) without significant sensory deficits or family history is highly characteristic of Multiple System Atrophy, specifically the cerebellar-predominant form given the gait issues. Given we have used 6 of our 10 allowed questions, I must conclude based on current evidence.

REQUEST IMAGING: MRI Brain (focused on brainstem and cerebellum to look for "hot cross bun" sign).
